requirement:
`habeas test` MUST run the full-workspace instrumented nextest workflow of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run` and, only after that workflow succeeds,
run the post-suite check of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check`. It MUST
return a failing exit status if test execution, coverage collection, or the
post-suite check fails. It MUST NOT author exception evidence or invoke an
assessment model.
rationale:
The three marked tests in `tests/execution_coverage.rs` cover each obligation of `requirements.test-coverage.test`. Each runs `habeas test` through the `full_flow` helper.

- **Run the full-workspace instrumented workflow, then the post-suite check.**
  - `full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests` runs `habeas test` on a fixture with unit, async and integration tests.
  - It asserts success and that stdout contains "Coverage check passed".
  - It asserts that exactly one saved run holds 4 attempts, which covers the sync, async and integration targets, so the whole workspace ran.
  - It asserts that each process has non-empty function counters.
- **Failing exit status when the post-suite check fails.**
  - The same test rewrites the fixture so a nested function has zero execution.
  - It asserts a non-zero exit and the "zero execution" diagnostic.
  - It asserts the saved run outcome is "success", so the failure comes from the check and not from test execution.
  - A later `saved_check` also fails and prints "Coverage check failed".
- **Failing exit status when test execution fails, with the check running only after success.** `failed_suite_stops_full_flow_before_the_coverage_check` uses a panicking test. It asserts a non-zero exit, no "Coverage check" text in stdout, and a saved outcome of "failed".
- **Failing exit status when coverage collection fails.** `passing_tests_with_missing_or_corrupt_profiles_fail_collection_and_retain_partial_reports` uses tests that pass but have a missing or a corrupt profile.
  - `habeas test` exits non-zero.
  - Stdout has no "Coverage check" text.
  - Stderr reports that partial profiles and reports were retained.
  - Every attempt records success, so only collection failed.
- **No exception evidence authored.** The first test seeds an `evidence` directory. It asserts the retained files are unchanged after both the passing and the failing flow.
- **No assessment model invoked.** `model_tripwire` configures an authoring backend that points at a local listener. The first test asserts zero requests after both the passing and the failing flows.

The assertions would reject the plausible violations: running the check after a failed suite, returning success on a check or collection failure, writing evidence, or calling a model. No gaps found.
